_note: How the ground suits each arm, on top of the classic battle rules, and what tanks and infantry do for each other. The grand campaign only: the historical scenarios are settled by the classic rules alone. attack and defence are multipliers by unit kind and terrain; march is extra moves to enter that terrain on the advance (not along roads through ground held since before the month began).

says.plains: Open country: the best ground there is for tanks
says.desert: Open desert: tank country, with nothing to hide behind
says.forest: Forest: tanks cannot manoeuvre among the trees
says.hills: Hill country: slow going for armour, good ground for mountain troops
says.mountain: Mountains: made for mountain troops, hard on anything with wheels or tracks
says.marsh: Marsh: the ground will not bear tanks, lorries or guns
says.urban: City streets: a fight for infantry, and no place for horses
says.steep: High mountains: too steep for tanks, and little better for lorries and guns
